title: Harold West's early death and Clyde Hart's tuberculosis
summary: Leeman says West died young from drug overdoses, and Clyde Hart, who was sick with tuberculosis, died the night after the Three Deuces engagement.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: First I'd like to say in relation to

our conversation the other day about drugs, and abuse and alcohol and so forth, it's neither her nor there, but I would like to mention that the aforementioned Harold West never reached his peak because of an early death by overdoses and using heavy drugs.
He was just one among many that I couldn't think of the other day while we were discussing the subject.

Another aside -- Clyde Hart died while we were on that engagement with the Three Deuces, and he had tuberculosis, which I didn't know. But he was very sick all the time he was playing, and I helped put him in a cab one morning after we got through playing, and he said, 'No, I'll get uptown all right, somebody is meeting me.' And I never saw him again -- he died during the night.
